findings.title: Qualify full-vocabulary recovery for metadata-free native checkpoints
findings.description: The guide says native loading always preserves the complete source vocabulary, including rows beyond tokenizer length. That guarantee holds for HF sources and metadata-bearing native Levanter checkpoints. For a metadata-free native checkpoint the shared loader keeps the Vocab supplied by this entrypoint, which is derived only from len(tokenizer) and rounded for compute placement. There is no independent source-vocabulary override here. For example, a metadata-free stored48/tokenizer47 source on a one-device mesh cannot recover the stored48 model vocabulary automatically. Qualify the guarantee and state that metadata-free checkpoints require the original native config and a rounded tokenizer vocabulary equal to the full stored vocabulary; semantic identity cannot be verified from same-shaped weights.

native-jax-trace-eval-guide-cold-read.md.text:
Cold read of the excerpt only, as a Marin user unfamiliar with this entrypoint:

- “Named Llama and `llama_native` configurations” does not identify the actual configuration field, accepted name(s), or how to invoke the module. One minimal command/config example would make the entrypoint usable.
- “Trace-labeled” and “labeled losses” are undefined: what supplies the labels, what input dataset format is expected, and is each reported loss grouped by label or attached to an individual trace?
- `checkpoint_is_hf` names a switch but the checkpoint-path and tokenizer/model configuration fields are absent. “Matching model architecture” leaves unclear whether an HF directory supplies architecture metadata or the user must specify it independently.
- “Native loading” has an unclear boundary: does it mean `llama_native`, a Levanter-format checkpoint, or both? That affects how to interpret the vocabulary-preservation claim.
- “Uses explicit mesh axes with the trainer's parameter storage and computation mappings” does not say whether these settings are inherited automatically or must be supplied by the user. Only the batch-axis field is concrete.
- “Rerunning the same configuration and output skips completed datasets” leaves resume safety unclear: does the evaluator check configuration identity, or must the user ensure that an existing results file belongs to the current configuration? Also unclear whether changing model/tokenizer/dataset settings requires a fresh output path.

native-jax-trace-eval-guide-r2-cold-read.text:
All three remaining concrete clarity points are resolved in this wording:

- “Haliax-based `LlamaConfig`” removes the ambiguous “named” terminology.
- The adapter sentence identifies patch text and the CORRECT/INCORRECT outcome token as appended labeled targets derived from row fields.
- The resume guidance names `max_eval_length` explicitly.

No remaining issues within the requested recheck scope. Prior notes preserved; no source lookup or draft edits.
